name: Oswald Wirth Tarot — The 22 Esoteric Arcana (1889 / 1926)
description:
# Oswald Wirth Tarot

## At a glance

The **first tarot conceived as an explicitly occult, initiatic instrument** (distinct from Etteilla's earlier *divination* deck of 1788) — 22 Major Arcana only, designed in **1889** by
**Oswald Wirth** under the direction of the Kabbalist **Stanislas de Guaita**, realising
the program of **Éliphas Lévi**. It fixes the marriage of tarot trumps to the **Hebrew
alphabet** and the Kabbalah that defines Continental (and later English) esoteric tarot.

## Origin & dating

Wirth, immersed in the French Occult Revival, was commissioned by de Guaita to draw 22
trumps "restored to hieroglyphic purity" per Lévi's ideas. Published **1889** as *Les 22
Arcanes du Tarot Kabbalistique* (hand-colored, gilt-edged like a grimoire). Wirth issued
a revised, wider-known version in **1926**. It reinterprets the **Marseille** trumps
through Kabbalah, alchemy, Hermeticism and Masonic/Rosicrucian symbolism.

## Provenance & evidence

The 1889 and 1926 decks and Wirth's accompanying writings survive. The lineage is
explicit and documented: **Lévi → de Guaita → Wirth**, the French esoteric current that
Lévi launched in the 1850s by asserting a tarot-Kabbalah correspondence.

## Game or divination?

**Esoteric/divinatory by design** — never a game deck. Note it is **trumps only** (22
cards): a philosophical/meditative object, the Continental sibling of what the Golden
Dawn was doing in England.

## The fear question

**Openly published, but inside a subculture.** Wirth and de Guaita were public figures of
a fashionable Parisian occult *movement* (salons, orders, presses). There was no legal
peril for these bourgeois esotericists; the "secrecy" was the deliberate mystique of
initiatory orders, not fear of prosecution. Contrast again the jobbing fortune-teller:
respectable occult *philosophy* was safe; commercial *fortune-telling* was the
criminalised, déclassé version of the same impulse.

## Counter-voices

Wirth's deck embodies the esoteric tradition's own self-understanding: that it is
*restoring* ancient symbolic truth (Lévi's Kabbalah-tarot link). The historical caveat:
Lévi's Hebrew-letter assignment was an **invention of the 1850s**, not a medieval
survival. But unlike the Egyptian myth, the Wirth deck is honest about being a
*construction* — it openly builds a new symbolic system on the Marseille, which is
exactly what the grammar should record (a deliberate esoteric overlay, well documented,
not a false antiquity claim).

## Open questions / corrections owed

- Distinguish the 1889 and 1926 versions in the grammar (de Guaita-directed vs. Wirth's
  mature revision).
- Wirth's Hebrew-letter/path assignments differ from the Golden Dawn's — do **not**
  conflate the two correspondence systems.

## Sources & further reading

- "Oswald Wirth Tarot," Wikipedia; "The Oswald Wirth Tarot," designdcl / tarotator.
- Stanislas de Guaita and Éliphas Lévi primary materials (public domain).

## One source per deck

This deck reads Wirth's 22 plates through **Wirth's own commentary** and nothing else.
**Papus's** *Le Tarot des Bohémiens* (1889), which used to sit on every card here, is now
its own deck — `papus-tarot-des-bohemiens` — illustrated with these same plates, since
Papus's book reproduced them. Same pictures, a different book about them.

## Wirth's own words (1927)

Each card carries two passages from Wirth's *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), in French with page numbers and this site's English translation: the opening of his chapter on the card, and his *Interprétations divinatoires*. The French is from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874), in the public domain (Wirth died in 1943). An earlier version of this deck carried English passages labelled as translated from this book; checked against the 1927 text, they were not Wirth's words (one called the Death card unnumbered, another made the Fool a sage), and they have been replaced. Later editions (the 1966 French reissue, the 1985 English translation *The Tarot of the Magicians*) are not quoted here. Wirth counts the Fool as the 22nd arcanum, with the value zero (p. 222).

Why Wirth kept divination in a book about symbols, in his words (p. 100):

> Envisagée comme exercice d'assouplissement de l'esprit, la divination a l'immense mérite d'obliger le devin à penser par lui-même, en l'astreignant à deviner, donc à sonder l'obscurité, pour y distinguer ce qui s'y cache.

*This site's translation:* Seen as an exercise that limbers the mind, divination has the great merit of obliging the diviner to think for himself, by compelling him to guess, and so to sound the darkness and make out what is hidden there.

sections.Symbolism: A wanderer in motley strides forward, a bundle on a staff, while a creature tears at his leg and a crocodile waits ahead. Wirth places the Fool between Judgement and the World — the unnumbered force of irrational, ungovernable spirit that animates the whole sequence.

sections.Divinatory meanings (Wirth, 1927):
*Wirth's Interprétations divinatoires:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), pp. 225–226 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation. Wirth runs each card from its highest sense down to its failings ("Partant du ciel, nous aboutissons à l'enfer", p. 100) and gives no reversed meanings.

> Parabrahm, Apsou, l'Abîme sans fond, l'Absolu, l'Infini, Ensoph. Ce qui dépasse notre compréhension. L'Irrationnel, l'Absurde. Le Vide, le Néant, la Nuit cosmogonique. La substance primordiale. Désintégration, anéantissement spirituel. Nirvahna.
>
> Passivité, impulsivité, abandon aux instincts aveugles, aux appétits et aux passions. Irresponsabilité, aliénation, folie. Inaptitude à se diriger, incapacité de résister aux influences subies. Médiumnité, sujétion, perte du libre-arbitre. Esclavage.
>
> Nullité. Jouet des forces occultes. Déséquilibré influençable. Sujet hypnotique. Instrument d'autrui. Inconscience. Profane non initiable. Aveugle entraîné à sa perte. Insensé s'abandonnant à ses lubies. Insensibilité, indifférence, nonchalance. Incapacité de reconnaître ses torts et d'en éprouver du remords.

**This site's translation**

Parabrahm, Apsu, the bottomless Abyss, the Absolute, the Infinite, Ein Soph. What passes our understanding. The Irrational, the Absurd. The Void, Nothingness, the cosmogonic Night. The primordial substance. Disintegration, spiritual annihilation. Nirvana.

Passivity, impulsiveness, surrender to blind instincts, to appetites and passions. Irresponsibility, alienation, madness. Inability to steer oneself, incapacity to resist the influences one undergoes. Mediumship, subjection, loss of free will. Slavery.

Nullity. Plaything of occult forces. An unbalanced person easily swayed. Hypnotic subject. Another's instrument. Unconsciousness. A profane who cannot be initiated. A blind man led to his ruin. A madman giving himself up to his whims. Insensibility, indifference, nonchalance. Inability to recognise one's wrongs and to feel remorse for them.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Keeps the Marseille *Mat* (unnumbered vagabond) and assigns **ש Shin ("tooth, fire")** — Lévi was **the first to link the Fool with Shin**, and Wirth follows him [@web_levi_arrangement; @hermetics_marathakis]. **Critical placement point:** in **Lévi's and Wirth's scheme the Fool is unnumbered and sits between Trump XX (Judgement) and Trump XXI (The World)** — it is *not* "card 0" at the head of the deck. That Fool-first-as-0 = Aleph arrangement is the **Golden Dawn's** different system. *(The grammar lists Le Fou at sort_order 0 with Shin; the letter is right but the position implies the Golden Dawn order — flag.)* [@web_levi_arrangement; @web_gd_swap]. 

*Sources:* [@hermetics_marathakis], [@web_gd_swap], [@web_levi_arrangement].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/oswald-wirth-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/oswald-wirth-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol:
The Fool as pure spirit: undifferentiated potential, Ain Soph (the limitless), associated with the element of Air and the Hebrew letter Shin. Wirth placed him unnumbered at the threshold between the Major Arcana.

*Editorial note, not Wirth's words. Planet and zodiac links here come partly from later systems; Wirth's own letter and constellations are under Correspondences.*
sections.Wirth:
*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter XXII. Le Fou, p. 222 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> L'ordre des arcanes des anciens Tarots est marqué en chiffres romains de I à XXI ; puis vient une dernière composition qui se distingue des autres par l'omission de toute indication numérale. Son rang est le vingt-deuxième, mais sa valeur symbolique équivaut à zéro, car le Fou est le personnage qui ne compte pas, vu son inexistence intellectuelle et morale. Inconscient et irresponsable, il se traîne à travers la vie en être passif, qui ne sait où il va et se laisse mener par les impulsions irraisonnées. Ne s'appartenant pas à lui-même, il est possédé : c'est un aliéné dans toute la force du terme.

**This site's translation**

In the old Tarots the order of the arcana is marked in Roman numerals from I to XXI; then comes a last composition, set apart from the others by the absence of any number. Its rank is the twenty-second, but its symbolic value equals zero, for the Fool is the figure who does not count, given his intellectual and moral non-existence. Unconscious and irresponsible, he drags himself through life as a passive being who does not know where he is going and lets himself be led by unreasoned impulses. Not belonging to himself, he is possessed: he is alienated in the full force of the word.

sections.Divinatory meanings (Wirth, 1927):
*Wirth's Interprétations divinatoires:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), p. 104 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation. Wirth runs each card from its highest sense down to its failings ("Partant du ciel, nous aboutissons à l'enfer", p. 100) and gives no reversed meanings.

> Kéther, la Couronne de l'Arbre des Séphiroth. Le commencement de toutes choses : Cause première, Unité-Principe, Esprit pur, Sujet pensant unique et universel, se réfractant dans le Moi de toute créature intelligente.
>
> Initiative, centre d'action, spontanéité d'intelligence, acuité de discernement et de compréhension, présence d'esprit, possession de soi, autonomie, rejet de toute suggestion étrangère, émancipation de tout préjugé.
>
> Dextérité, habileté, finesse diplomatique. Hableur persuasif, avocat ; ruse, astuce, agitation. Absence de scrupules, arriviste, intrigant, menteur, coquin, escroc, charlatan, exploiteur de la candeur humaine. — Influence de Mercure en bien comme en mal.

**This site's translation**

Kether, the Crown of the Tree of the Sephiroth. The beginning of all things: First Cause, Unity-as-Principle, pure Spirit, the single and universal thinking Subject, refracted in the Self of every intelligent creature.

Initiative, a centre of action, quickness of mind, sharp discernment and understanding, presence of mind, self-possession, autonomy, refusal of every suggestion from outside, freedom from all prejudice.

Dexterity, skill, diplomatic finesse. A persuasive talker, a lawyer; guile, cunning, restlessness. Lack of scruples; a careerist, a schemer, a liar, a rogue, a swindler, a charlatan, one who exploits human candour. — The influence of Mercury, for good and for ill.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Marseille's *Bateleur* is a fairground conjuror; Wirth makes him the **human will gathering the four elements**, adds the **lemniscate** of eternal force, and assigns him **א Aleph ("ox"), the first letter** — because Lévi held "his body and arms constitute the letter Aleph," the seed of the whole trump↔alphabet scheme [@hermetics_marathakis; @web_levi_arrangement]. In the **1926** redraw the wand's blue/red ends are inverted and the table carries **one** object rather than three [@web_cartomancer]. 

*Sources:* [@hermetics_marathakis], [@web_cartomancer], [@web_levi_arrangement], [@web_wirth_wp].

sections.Wirth:
*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter I. Le Bateleur, p. 101 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Comment un escamoteur a-t-il pu être placé en tête du Tarot, marqué du nombre Un, qui est celui de la Cause première ? Au tome VIII de son Monde Primitif, Court de Gebelin estime le choix de ce personnage essentiellement philosophique. L'Univers visible n'étant que magie et prestige, son Créateur ne serait-il pas l'Illusionniste par excellence, le grand Prestidigitateur qui nous éblouit par ses tours de passe-passe ? Le tourbillonnement universel des choses nous empêche de percevoir la réalité : nous sommes le jouet d'apparences produites par le jeu de forces qui nous sont inconnues.
>
> La Cause première est donc un Bateleur ; mais comme elle se répercute en tout ce qui est actif, le personnage initial du Tarot correspond, d'une manière générale, à tout principe d'activité. Dans l'Univers, c'est Dieu, envisagé comme le grand suggestionneur de tout ce qui s'accomplit dans le Cosmos ; dans l'homme c'est le foyer de l'initiative individuelle, centre de perception, de conscience et de volonté ; c'est le Moi appelé à créer notre personnalité, car l'individu a mission de se faire lui-même.

**This site's translation**

How could a conjuror have been placed at the head of the Tarot, marked with the number One, which is the number of the First Cause? In volume VIII of his Monde Primitif, Court de Gébelin judges the choice of this figure to be essentially philosophical. Since the visible Universe is nothing but magic and glamour, would its Creator not be the Illusionist par excellence, the great Prestidigitator who dazzles us with his sleights of hand? The universal whirling of things keeps us from perceiving reality: we are the plaything of appearances produced by the play of forces unknown to us.

The First Cause is therefore a Juggler; but since it echoes in everything that is active, the opening figure of the Tarot corresponds, in a general way, to every principle of activity. In the Universe it is God, seen as the great suggester of all that is accomplished in the Cosmos; in the human being it is the hearth of individual initiative, the centre of perception, of consciousness and of will; it is the Self called to create our personality, for the individual has the mission of making himself.

sections.Divinatory meanings (Wirth, 1927):
*Wirth's Interprétations divinatoires:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), pp. 108–109 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation. Wirth runs each card from its highest sense down to its failings ("Partant du ciel, nous aboutissons à l'enfer", p. 100) and gives no reversed meanings.

> C'Hocmah, la Sagesse, la Pensée créatrice, le Verbe, seconde personne de la Trinité, Isis, la Nature, épouse de Dieu et mère de toutes choses. La substance qui remplit l'espace illimité ; le champ d'action de la cause active et intelligente. L'opposition féconde dont tout s'engendre. La différentiation qui permet de distinguer, de percevoir, donc de connaître et de savoir.
>
> La Science sacrée, dont l'objet ne tombe pas sous les sens. Divination, Philosophie intuitive, Gnose, discernement du mystère, Religion spontanée, Foi contemplative.
>
> Silence, discrétion, réserve, méditation. Modestie, patience, résignation, piété, respect des choses saintes. — Dissimulation, intentions cachées, rancune, inertie, paresse, bigoterie, intolérance, fanatisme. Influence saturnienne passive.

**This site's translation**

Chokmah, Wisdom, creative Thought, the Word, second person of the Trinity, Isis, Nature, spouse of God and mother of all things. The substance that fills boundless space; the field in which the active, intelligent cause works. The fertile opposition from which everything is born. The differentiation that lets us distinguish and perceive, and so know.

Sacred Science, whose object is not perceived by the senses. Divination, intuitive Philosophy, Gnosis, discernment of mystery, spontaneous Religion, contemplative Faith.

Silence, discretion, reserve, meditation. Modesty, patience, resignation, piety, respect for holy things. — Dissimulation, hidden intentions, rancour, inertia, laziness, bigotry, intolerance, fanaticism. A passive Saturnian influence.

sections.Wirth:
*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter II. La Papesse, p. 105 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Personnification de la cause initiale de toute action, le Bateleur (Arc. I) se trémousse et ne peut rester en repos, aussi est-il représenté debout, à l'encontre de la Papesse (Arc. II), qui est assise dans une immobilité calme, silencieuse, impénétrable et hiératique. Elle est la prêtresse du mystère, Isis, la déesse de la nuit profonde que l'esprit humain ne saurait pénétrer sans son secours.
>
> Sa droite entr'ouvre le livre des secrets que nul ne peut surprendre, si la Papesse ne lui confie les clefs qu'elle tient en sa main gauche. De ces clefs qui ouvrent l'intérieur des choses (Ésotérisme), l'une est d'or et se rapporte au Soleil (Verbe, Raison) et l'autre d'argent, donc en affinité avec la Lune (Imagination, lucidité intuitive). Cela signifie qu'il faut allier une sévère logique à une exquise impressionnabilité, si l'on aspire à deviner les choses cachées, celles dont la Nature dérobe la connaissance au grand nombre.

**This site's translation**

The Juggler (Arc. I), personification of the first cause of all action, fidgets and cannot keep still, and so he is shown standing, unlike the Popess (Arc. II), who is seated in a calm, silent, impenetrable and hieratic stillness. She is the priestess of mystery, Isis, goddess of the deep night that the human mind could not enter without her help.

Her right hand half-opens the book of secrets that no one can come upon unless the Popess entrusts them with the keys she holds in her left hand. Of these keys, which open the inside of things (Esotericism), one is gold and relates to the Sun (the Word, Reason) and the other silver, and so akin to the Moon (Imagination, intuitive clarity). This means that a strict logic must be joined to an exquisite sensitivity if one hopes to divine hidden things, the things whose knowledge Nature keeps from the many.

The domain of what can be known and understood. Discernment, reflection, study, observation, inductive science. Education, knowledge, learning.

Affability, grace, charm, strength of soul, rule exercised through gentleness, a civilising influence. Courtesy, generosity. Abundance, wealth, fertility.

Pomp, vanity, frivolity, luxury, extravagance, coquetry, seduction, a display of superficial notions, posing, affectation.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter III. L'Impératrice, p. 110 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> L'Unité nécessaire et fondamentale des choses (Arc. I) s'impose à notre esprit sans se rendre intelligible. Nous ne pouvons nous représenter ce qui est illimité, infini, indéterminé, si ce n'est en évoquant l'image d'une nuit aux insondables profondeurs, domaine d'Isis, la déesse du Mystère, dont la Papesse (Arc. II) est la grande prêtresse. Mais notre pensée s'efforce en vain de plonger dans l'Abîme sans fond des cosmogonies (Apsou des Chaldéens) ; elle n'y perçoit qu'un chaos mental devant lequel nous restons effarés, saisis de terreur religieuse et condamnés au mutisme. Pour tirer notre esprit de la confusion, il lui faut l'aide de l'Impératrice du Tarot.
>
> Cette souveraine resplendissante de clarté figure l'Intelligence créatrice, mère des formes, des images et des idées. C'est la Vierge immaculée des Chrétiens, en qui les Grecs auraient reconnu leur Vénus-Uranie, née radieuse des sombres flots de l'Océan chaotique.

**This site's translation**

The necessary and fundamental Unity of things (Arc. I) forces itself on our mind without becoming intelligible. We cannot picture what is unlimited, infinite, undetermined, except by calling up the image of a night of unfathomable depths, the domain of Isis, goddess of Mystery, whose high priestess is the Popess (Arc. II). But our thought tries in vain to plunge into the bottomless Abyss of the cosmogonies (the Apsu of the Chaldeans); it sees there only a mental chaos before which we stand aghast, seized with religious terror and condemned to silence. To draw our mind out of confusion, it needs the help of the Empress of the Tarot.

This sovereign, resplendent with light, stands for creative Intelligence, mother of forms, images and ideas. She is the immaculate Virgin of the Christians, in whom the Greeks would have recognised their Venus Urania, born radiant from the dark waves of the chaotic Ocean.

The Emperor is indeed the Prince of this World; he reigns over the concrete, over what has taken bodily form, hence the contrast between his lower empire, and so infernal in the etymological sense of the word, and the heavenly rule of the Empress, exercised directly over souls and pure spirits.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter V. Le Pape, p. 120 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Les artistes qui ont dessiné le Tarot se plaisaient aux contrastes. Auprès du Bateleur juvénile et blond qui se démène debout, ils ont placé la ténébreuse Papesse, assise et enveloppée de mystère ; puis vient l'Impératrice radiante de clarté céleste et se montrant rigoureusement de face, pour mieux se différencier de l'Empereur au profil sévère et à la barbe noire. La mine renfrognée de ce souverain fait apprécier, à son tour, le visage jovial et plein d'aménité du Pape. Ce pontife au teint fleuri et aux joues pleines est, certes, plein d'indulgence pour les faiblesses humaines. Il comprend tout, car rien n'échappe au paisible regard de ses yeux bleus très clairs, qu'ombragent à peine d'épais sourcils blancs.

**This site's translation**

The artists who drew the Tarot delighted in contrasts. Beside the young, fair Juggler bustling on his feet they set the dark Popess, seated and wrapped in mystery; then comes the Empress, radiant with heavenly light and shown strictly full face, the better to set her apart from the Emperor with his stern profile and black beard. The scowl of that sovereign in turn makes us value the jovial and kindly face of the Pope. This pontiff, ruddy and full-cheeked, is certainly full of indulgence for human weaknesses. He understands everything, for nothing escapes the calm gaze of his very pale blue eyes, barely shaded by thick white brows.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter VI. L'Amoureux, p. 127 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Au sortir de l'adolescence, alors qu'il venait d'achever son éducation à l'école du Centaure Chiron (Apprentissage initiatique), Hercule éprouva le besoin de réfléchir à l'emploi qu'il ferait, dans la vie, de ses puissantes facultés développées à souhait. S'étant enfoncé dans la solitude, afin de s'y recueillir, deux femmes d'une rare beauté lui apparurent soudain, l'incitant chacune à la suivre. La première, la Vertu, lui fit entrevoir une existence de lutte, d'efforts incessants, en vue du triomphe par le courage et l'énergie. L'autre, la Mollesse, pour ne pas dire le Vice, engagea le jeune homme à jouir paisiblement de la vie, en s'abandonnant à ses douceurs et en profitant des avantages qu'elle offre à qui sait borner son ambition.
>
> S'inspirant de cette scène mythologique, la sixième clef du Tarot nous montre un jouvenceau arrêté à l'intersection de deux routes, les bras croisés sur la poitrine, le regard baissé, incertain de la direction à suivre.

**This site's translation**

On leaving adolescence, having just finished his education in the school of the Centaur Chiron (initiatory Apprenticeship), Hercules felt the need to reflect on what use he would make, in life, of his powerful faculties, now fully developed. He had gone deep into solitude to gather himself when two women of rare beauty suddenly appeared to him, each urging him to follow her. The first, Virtue, showed him a life of struggle and ceaseless effort, aimed at triumph through courage and energy. The other, Softness, not to say Vice, invited the young man to enjoy life peacefully, giving himself up to its pleasures and taking the advantages it offers to anyone who knows how to limit his ambition.

Drawing on this mythological scene, the sixth key of the Tarot shows us a youth halted where two roads cross, arms folded over his chest, eyes lowered, unsure which way to go.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter VII. Le Chariot, p. 131 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> On peut se demander si le titre d'un traité d'Alchimie, paru à Amsterdam en 1671, ne nous révèle pas la vraie désignation de la 7e clef du Tarot. En ce cas, le Chariot deviendrait le Char triomphal de l'Antimoine, le Currus triumphalis Antimonii de Basile Valentin. Ce qui est certain, c'est que l'Antimoine est fort bien représenté par le maître du Chariot. Ce jeune homme imberbe, svelte, blond comme le Bateleur et l'Amoureux, est revêtu d'une cuirasse et armé d'un sceptre comme l'Empereur. Il incarne les principes supérieurs de la personnalité humaine pour représenter l'Ame intellectuelle, en laquelle se synthétisent le Principe pensant (Bateleur), le Centre d'énergie volitive (Empereur) et le foyer d'où rayonne l'affection (Amoureux).

**This site's translation**

One may wonder whether the title of a treatise on Alchemy, published in Amsterdam in 1671, does not reveal the true name of the 7th key of the Tarot. In that case the Chariot would become the Triumphal Chariot of Antimony, the Currus triumphalis Antimonii of Basil Valentine. What is certain is that Antimony is very well represented by the master of the Chariot. This beardless young man, slender and fair like the Juggler and the Lover, wears a breastplate and carries a sceptre like the Emperor. He embodies the higher principles of the human personality, standing for the intellectual Soul, in which are joined the thinking Principle (the Juggler), the Centre of willing energy (the Emperor) and the hearth from which affection radiates (the Lover).

> Le premier chapitre du livre d'Ezéchiel décrit une vision sur laquelle ont disserté à perte de vue d'innombrables kabbalistes. Les cieux s'étant ouverts, le prophète y vit des animaux étranges groupés par quatre et près d'eux un quaternaire de roues de feu, dont chacune était double. La 10e clef du Tarot, dont le symbolisme a été fixé par Eliphas Lévi, s'inspire du texte sacré lorsqu'elle nous montre une roue à deux jantes concentriques, image du double tourbillon générateur de la vie individuelle.
>
> Cette vie s'engendre à la façon d'un courant électrique, dès qu'un tourbillonnement restreint s'établit en sens contraire du mouvement giratoire enveloppant. L'individu résulte d'une opposition au tout dont il fait partie. Il ne se fait centre qu'en s'insurgeant contre l'universalité.

**This site's translation**

The first chapter of the book of Ezekiel describes a vision on which countless Kabbalists have discoursed without end. The heavens opened, and the prophet saw strange creatures grouped in fours and, near them, four wheels of fire, each of them double. The 10th key of the Tarot, whose symbolism was fixed by Eliphas Lévi, draws on the sacred text when it shows us a wheel with two concentric rims, an image of the double vortex that generates individual life.

This life is generated in the manner of an electric current, as soon as a small whirling sets itself up against the surrounding rotation. The individual results from an opposition to the whole of which it is a part. It makes itself a centre only by rising against universality.

> L'énergie suprême, à laquelle ne résiste aucune brutalité, se présente dans le Tarot sous l'aspect d'une reine blonde et gracieuse, qui, sans effort apparent, dompte un lion furieux, dont elle maintient les mâchoires écartées. Cette conception de la Force, en tant que vertu cardinale, s'écarte des figurations banales d'un Hercule appuyé sur sa massue et revêtu de la dépouille du lion de Némée. Ce n'est point la vigueur physique, celle des muscles, que glorifie l'arcane XI ; il s'agit de l'exercice d'une puissance féminine, bien plus irrésistible dans sa douceur et sa subtilité que toutes les explosions de la colère et de la force brutale.

**This site's translation**

The supreme energy, which no brutality can resist, appears in the Tarot as a fair and graceful queen who, with no visible effort, masters a raging lion and holds its jaws apart. This idea of Strength as a cardinal virtue departs from the commonplace pictures of a Hercules leaning on his club and dressed in the skin of the Nemean lion. Arcanum XI does not glorify physical vigour, the strength of muscles; it concerns the exercise of a feminine power, far more irresistible in its gentleness and subtlety than all the outbursts of anger and brute force.

> […] le Tarot ne s'arrête pas à l'arcane XI ; mais avec XII, il aborde un domaine entièrement différent, qui est celui de l'Initiation passive ou mystique, dite aussi féminine ou ionienne. Désormais la personnalité renonce à l'exaltation des énergies propres ; loin de se comporter en centre d'action autonome, elle s'efface pour subir docilement les influences extérieures. Le Mage a foi en lui-même, en son intelligence et en sa volonté ; il se sent souverain et aspire à conquérir son royaume. Le Mystique se persuade, au contraire, qu'il n'est rien, sinon une coque vide, impuissante par elle-même. Son renoncement passif le met à la disposition de ce qui agit sur lui. Il se livre pied et bras liés, comme le Pendu, qui, dans le Tarot, semble être le même personnage que le Bateleur.

**This site's translation**

[…] the Tarot does not stop at arcanum XI; with XII it enters an entirely different domain, that of passive or mystical Initiation, also called feminine or Ionian. From here on the personality gives up exalting its own energies; far from acting as an autonomous centre of action, it steps aside in order to undergo outside influences docilely. The Magus has faith in himself, in his intelligence and his will; he feels himself sovereign and aspires to conquer his kingdom. The Mystic, on the contrary, persuades himself that he is nothing but an empty shell, powerless in himself. His passive renunciation places him at the disposal of whatever acts upon him. He gives himself up bound hand and foot, like the Hanged Man, who in the Tarot seems to be the same figure as the Juggler.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter XIII. La Mort, p. 163 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Les compositions du Tarot portent leur désignation tracée en toutes lettres : Bateleur, Papesse, Impératrice, etc... Seul l'arcane XIII reste intentionnellement muet, comme s'il avait répugné aux imagiers du Moyen-Age de nommer le squelette faucheur dont la moisson se compose de têtes humaines. Auraient-ils donc refusé de ne voir que la Mort en l'universel destructeur des formes périssables ? Considérant la Vie comme seule existante, il semble qu'ils n'aient cru ni à la Mort, ni au Néant. Ce qui est change d'aspect, mais ne se détruit jamais : tout persiste en se modifiant indéfiniment sous l'action du grand transformateur auquel les êtres individuels doivent leur origine. En dissolvant les formes usées devenues incapables de répondre à leur destination, cet agent intervient comme rajeunisseur, puisqu'il libère les énergies destinées à entrer en de nouvelles combinaisons vitales. Nous devons notre existence éphémère à ce que nous appelons la Mort. Elle nous permit de naître et ne peut nous conduire qu'à une renaissance.

**This site's translation**

The compositions of the Tarot carry their names written out in full: Juggler, Popess, Empress, and so on. Arcanum XIII alone remains deliberately mute, as if the image-makers of the Middle Ages had been loath to name the reaping skeleton whose harvest is made of human heads. Did they then refuse to see nothing but Death in the universal destroyer of perishable forms? Holding Life to be the only thing that exists, they seem to have believed neither in Death nor in Nothingness. What is changes its appearance but is never destroyed: everything persists, endlessly modified by the great transformer to which individual beings owe their origin. By dissolving worn-out forms that can no longer serve their purpose, this agent acts as a rejuvenator, since it frees the energies destined to enter new living combinations. We owe our brief existence to what we call Death. It allowed us to be born and can lead us only to a rebirth.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter XIIII. La Tempérance, p. 169 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Si l'Initiation enseigne à mourir, ce n'est pas pour préconiser l'anéantissement. Ce qui, de toute certitude, n'existe pas, c'est le Néant ! Y aspirer correspond à l'idéal le plus faux qui puisse se concevoir, car rien ne se détruit, tout se transforme. Loin de supprimer la vie, la mort pourvoit à son perpétuel rajeunissement. Elle dissout le contenant, afin de libérer le contenu, que l'on peut se représenter comme un liquide incessamment transvasé d'un récipient périssable en un autre, sans que jamais il s'en perde une goutte.
>
> La XIIIIe clef du Tarot nous montre ce fluide vital versé d'une urne d'argent dans une urne d'or par la Tempérance, qui devient l'ange de la Vie universelle.

**This site's translation**

If Initiation teaches how to die, it is not in order to recommend annihilation. What most certainly does not exist is Nothingness! To aspire to it is the falsest ideal that can be conceived, for nothing is destroyed, everything is transformed. Far from abolishing life, death provides for its perpetual renewal. It dissolves the container in order to free the contents, which we may picture as a liquid endlessly poured from one perishable vessel into another without a single drop ever being lost.

The 14th key of the Tarot shows us this vital fluid being poured from a silver urn into a golden urn by Temperance, who becomes the angel of universal Life.

*Wirth in his own words:* *Le Tarot des imagiers du Moyen Âge* (Paris: Le Symbolisme / Émile Nourry, 1927), chapter XV. Le Diable, p. 174 · public domain · French from the [BnF copy on Gallica](https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3112874) · the English below is this site's translation

> Envisagée dans son essence commune à tous les êtres, la vie universelle circule sans arrêt, toujours identique à elle-même en s'écoulant avec indifférence d'un récipient dans l'autre. Si rien ne venait troubler la régularité de cet écoulement paisible, la vie serait restée conforme à l'idéal paradisiaque ; mais le Serpent intervint, et, sous son inspiration, chaque être voulut accaparer le bien commun, pour condenser la vie autour de lui à son bénéfice individuel. Il y eut ainsi révolte contre l'ordre universel des choses. Des tourbillons particuliers prirent naissance au sein de la circulation générale, troublée par l'égoïsme radical, que personnifie le Diable. Cet Adversaire (Satan en hébreu) est le Prince du Monde matériel, qui, sans lui, ne saurait exister, car il est à la base de toute différentiation particularisante.

**This site's translation**

Seen in its essence, common to all beings, universal life circulates without pause, always identical to itself as it flows indifferently from one vessel into another. Had nothing come to disturb the regularity of this peaceful flow, life would have remained true to the ideal of paradise; but the Serpent intervened, and under its inspiration each being wanted to seize the common good and condense life around itself for its own individual benefit. So there was revolt against the universal order of things. Particular whirlpools arose within the general circulation, disturbed by the radical selfishness that the Devil personifies. This Adversary (Satan, in Hebrew) is the Prince of the material World, which could not exist without him, for he lies at the root of every differentiation into particulars.

Wirth runs each card from its highest sense down to its failings ("Partant du ciel, nous aboutissons à l'enfer", p. 100) and gives no reversed meanings.

> Matérialisation. Attract condensateur. Egoïsme radical en action. Accaparement restrictif. Esprit emprisonné dans la matière. Construction vitale dont résulte tout l'organisme.
>
> Orgueil, présomption, poursuite de chimères. Matérialisme qui s'attache aux apparences grossières, avidité d'acquérir, manie des richesses matérielles. Mégalomanie, extension abusive de ce que l'on possède. Ambitions et appétits insatiables. Conquêtes immodérées. Exploitation déraisonnable. Excès et abus poussant à la révolte et aux bouleversements. Dogmatisme étroit, source d'incrédulité.
>
> Alchimie ignorante des souffleurs avides d'or vulgaire. Echec mérité de toute entreprise insensée. Punition résultant d'excès commis. Maladie, désorganisation, encrassement, durcissement, pétrification de ce qui était souple et vivant. Ruine des empires constitués et maintenus par la force brutale. Effondrement des Eglises intolérantes qui se proclament infaillibles. Erreur du présomptueux qui entreprend au-dessus de ses forces et ne sait s'arrêter opportunément.
>
> Lorsque cet arcane cesse d'être défavorable, il met en garde contre ce dont il menace. Crainte salutaire, réserve, timidité préservatrice de risques inconsidérés ; simplicité d'esprit détournant de sottises savantes, bon sens vulgaire, sagesse de Sancho Pança.

**This site's translation**

Materialisation. A condensing attraction. Radical selfishness in action. Grasping and hoarding. Spirit imprisoned in matter. The living construction from which the whole organism results.

Pride, presumption, the pursuit of chimeras. A materialism that clings to coarse appearances, greed for acquiring, a mania for material wealth. Megalomania, abusive extension of what one owns. Insatiable ambitions and appetites. Immoderate conquests. Unreasonable exploitation. Excess and abuse that drive to revolt and upheaval. Narrow dogmatism, a source of unbelief.

The ignorant alchemy of the 'puffers' greedy for common gold. The deserved failure of every senseless undertaking. Punishment that follows from excesses committed. Illness, disorganisation, clogging, hardening, the petrifying of what was supple and alive. The ruin of empires built and held by brute force. The collapse of intolerant Churches that proclaim themselves infallible. The error of the presumptuous one who undertakes more than his strength allows and does not know when to stop.

When this arcanum ceases to be unfavourable, it warns against what it threatens. A salutary fear, reserve, a timidity that protects from rash risks; a simplicity of mind that turns one away from learned follies, plain common sense, the wisdom of Sancho Panza.

> La Tour de l'arcane XVI est le premier édifice qui se rencontre dans le Tarot, où des constructions analogues ne figurent plus que sous la Lune (XVIII). […]
>
> Il y a danger à s'élever trop haut, nous en sommes avertis par le trait de foudre parti du Soleil qui décapite la Tour. Le Soleil est le symbole de la Raison qui gouverne les hommes et s'oppose à leurs extravagances. Quand nous poursuivons une entreprise chimérique, la catastrophe est fatale, provoquée par notre faute, mais déterminée dans son accomplissement par l'action de la lumière qui éclaire les intelligences. Ce qui est déraisonnable se condamne soi-même à l'effondrement. Tant pis pour l'ambitieux qui se donne beaucoup de peine pour s'élever bien haut, sans se douter que les sommets attirent la foudre.

**This site's translation**

The Tower of arcanum XVI is the first building we meet in the Tarot, where similar structures appear again only under the Moon (XVIII). […]

There is danger in rising too high: we are warned of it by the bolt of lightning, sent from the Sun, that beheads the Tower. The Sun is the symbol of the Reason that governs human beings and opposes their extravagances. When we pursue a chimerical undertaking, catastrophe is bound to come, caused by our own fault but brought to completion by the action of the light that illumines minds. What is unreasonable condemns itself to collapse. So much the worse for the ambitious one who takes great pains to climb very high, never suspecting that summits draw the lightning.

What they reveal to us is tiny beside the unfathomable unknown that surrounds us. We are plunged in a deep night, but when we turn our eyes to the sky, we see the Stars twinkle.

> Pour déployer les splendeurs du ciel, la Nuit plonge la terre dans les ténèbres, car les choses d'en haut ne se révèlent à notre vue qu'au détriment de celles d'en bas. Cet astre, qui s'associe aux étoiles sans amortir totalement leur éclat, n'éclaire qu'à demi les objets que baigne son incertaine lumière d'emprunt. La Lune ne permet pas de distinguer les couleurs ; elle teinte de gris argenté ou de nuances bleutées indécises ce que frappent ses rayons, en laissant subsister ailleurs le noir opaque des ombres de la nuit.

**This site's translation**

To unfold the splendours of the sky, Night plunges the earth into darkness, for the things above reveal themselves to our sight only at the expense of the things below. Yet we long to join the heavenly to the earthly in a single act of contemplation, which becomes possible when the Moon spreads her pale light. This heavenly body, which keeps company with the stars without wholly dimming their brightness, only half lights the objects bathed in her uncertain, borrowed light. The Moon does not let us tell colours apart; she tints whatever her rays strike with silvery grey or vague bluish shades, and elsewhere leaves the opaque black of the night's shadows.

> Si resplendissante que soit la lumière solaire, elle s'arrête à la superficie des choses, sans parvenir à nous en révéler l'essence intime qui ne tombe pas sous les sens. Or les œuvres de pure beauté, qu'elles soient produites par la Nature ou par l'Art, traduisent en leur forme extérieure un ésotérisme, ou esprit intérieur caché, qu'il appartient à l'intelligence de discerner. Le Jugement intervient à cet effet pour distinguer le spirituel du matériel, le fond signifié de la forme expressive, le verbe vivant de la lettre morte. Tout est symbole, car tout procède d'une idée génératrice qui se rattache à des conceptions transcendantes. Pénétrons dans la profondeur des choses, où sommeille une pensée qui attend que notre esprit la réveille et se l'assimile.

**This site's translation**

However resplendent the light of the sun may be, it stops at the surface of things and cannot reveal their inner essence, which the senses do not reach. Now works of pure beauty, whether made by Nature or by Art, express in their outward form an esotericism, a hidden inner spirit, which it is for the intelligence to discern. Judgement comes in for this purpose: to tell the spiritual from the material, the meaning signified from the form that expresses it, the living word from the dead letter. Everything is a symbol, for everything proceeds from a generating idea tied to transcendent conceptions. Let us go down into the depth of things, where a thought lies sleeping, waiting for our mind to wake it and take it in.

sections.About the Sequence: For Wirth, following Eliphas Levi, the 22 trumps are not a random gallery but a single initiatory ladder mapped onto the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet and the paths of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life. The Magician's will descends through nature, authority, choice, and trial; is tested by the Wheel, Death, and the Tower; and is reborn through the Star, Sun, and Judgement to the completed World. The Fool moves through all of it as the ungovernable spirit.
sections.How to Read It: Trace the cards in order as the soul's progress, or pair them across the sequence (Magician and World, Popess and Moon, Empress and Star) to see Wirth's symmetries. This is esoteric tarot in its Continental form — the bridge from the medieval Marseille image to the English decks that followed.
sections.Symbol: Wirth's 22-card system, designed under the direction of Stanislas de Guaïta, sets the Hebrew alphabet on the trumps in Eliphas Lévi's order. The deck joins Marseille iconography to the French occultism of Lévi and his followers, not to the English Golden Dawn, whose letters differ; it shaped 20th-century tarot practice.
